description: The National Register of Health Establishments (CNES) is Brazil's national register of health facilities, from hospitals and clinics to laboratories and regulation centres, within the Unified Health System (SUS). It is maintained by the Ministry of Health through DATASUS, its information technology department, and published through the SUS open data API. Each establishment record gives its CNES code, tax number, legal and trade names, management and administrative sphere, unit type, full address, phone and email, latitude and longitude, opening shift, whether it offers SUS outpatient care, state and municipality codes, and flags for a surgical centre, obstetric centre, neonatal centre, hospital care, support services and outpatient care, with the date of last update. The data are free and available through the API as JSON, and the portal states a CC BY-ND 3.0 licence for its content. Caveats: the open API gives facility attributes but not bed counts or staff in the records read, coordinates come from the register and should be checked before use, and paging through the API is needed for a full national copy. Simulation uses: mapping hospitals and emergency-capable facilities for flood, landslide or heat exposure studies, building travel-time access models, and locating surgical and obstetric capacity for emergency planning. Related records: the Mexican CLUES catalogue (data-mexico-clues-health-establishments) and the Spanish hospital catalogue (data-spain-catalogo-nacional-hospitales) are comparable national registers.
